# How to avoid overbooking in a hotel: 6 steps across OTAs
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/blog/how-to-prevent-overbooking/

## How to avoid overbooking in a hotel: 6 steps across OTAs
By the Hostlio Pro product team , the people who build Hostlio Pro. Published September 21, 2026 , updated September 23, 2026

Short answer: Overbooking means accepting more reservations than you can host for the same room and dates. In independent hotels the most common cause is updating availability by hand on several OTAs. A two-way, real-time channel manager removes most of the risk.

Contents

- Why does overbooking happen?
- Prevent overbooking in 6 steps
- What if it happens anyway?
- Overbooking across OTA channels: where the gaps are
- A daily 5-minute overbooking check
- If it happens anyway: walking the guest
- How it works in Hostlio Pro

## Why does overbooking happen?

- Updating availability on Booking.com, Airbnb and Expedia separately, by hand
- Entering phone or walk-in bookings late
- Cancellations and changes reaching one channel but not another
- Delayed (hourly) sync between channels

## Prevent overbooking in 6 steps

- Use one source of availability. Every channel should read availability from one calendar (your PMS).

- Choose two-way, real-time sync. When a booking arrives, the room should close on other channels within seconds.

- Enter direct bookings immediately. Add phone and walk-in sales to the same calendar right away.

- Manage stop-sells and minimum stays in one place. Changing them channel by channel invites mistakes.

- Keep a small buffer in peak periods. Opening the last room only to your direct channel lowers the risk.

- Check channel mappings regularly. When you add a room type, confirm the mapping on every channel.

## What if it happens anyway?

Tell the guest promptly and honestly, offer an equal or better alternative (a nearby hotel, an upgrade) and cover extra costs such as transfers. Log which channel caused it and why.

## Overbooking across OTA channels: where the gaps are

Most double bookings at independent hotels don't come from one channel. They come from the gaps between channels:

- Calendar links instead of a connection. Syncing Airbnb or a smaller site through an iCal calendar link means availability is refreshed on a schedule, not the moment a booking arrives. Two guests can book the same night in that gap.

- Unmapped or wrongly mapped rooms. A new room type added on Booking.com but not mapped in the channel manager keeps selling on its own allotment.

- Changes made directly in an extranet. Opening rooms in one extranet by hand overrides what the channel manager sent, and the other channels never hear about it.

- Modifications and cancellations. A date change that reaches the PMS late leaves the old nights blocked and the new nights open everywhere.

- Rooms that can't actually be sold. A room with a broken air conditioner is still counted as available unless it is taken out of sale everywhere.
The fix is the same in every case: every channel reads availability from one calendar, over a direct two-way connection, and nothing changes availability outside that calendar. For the difference between the calendar and the connection, see PMS vs channel manager .

## A daily 5-minute overbooking check

- Look at today's and tomorrow's arrivals for any room with two bookings or a booking with no room.

- Check that yesterday's cancellations and modifications are on the calendar.

- Confirm the channel connection shows no sync errors.

- Take any room with a fault out of sale before you open the next season.

- After adding a room type or rate plan, check its mapping on every channel.

## If it happens anyway: walking the guest

Hotels call moving an overbooked guest to another property “walking the guest”. Done well, it can still end with a good review:

- Decide early. As soon as you spot the conflict, decide which booking you can honour. Don't wait for the guest to arrive.

- Find an equal or better room nearby and confirm it before you contact the guest.

- Cover the difference: the price gap, the transfer and, if possible, the first night.

- Tell the guest in their language, with the new address, how they'll get there and who to call.

- Offer to bring them back for the rest of the stay if you have a room from the next night.

- Log the cause (channel, room, mapping, manual change) so it doesn't repeat.
A message you can adapt:

Dear [name], we're very sorry: because of a booking error on our side we can't offer you the room you reserved for [dates]. We have booked you an equal room at [hotel], [distance] from us, and we will cover the price difference and your taxi there. Your new confirmation is attached. If you'd like to come back to us for the rest of your stay, we'll have your room ready from [date]. Please call us on [phone] with any question. [Your name], [Hotel]

## How it works in Hostlio Pro

Hostlio Pro's channel manager syncs availability two-way and in real time across 100+ channels over certified connections. Bookings appear on one room rack, colour-coded by channel.
Behind the scenes, the room rack runs a conflict check that lists double-booked and unassigned reservations and suggests a free room of the right type. Taking a room out of order drops its availability on every connected channel, the Today screen shows whether channels are in sync with a retry button, and “resend to channels” pushes current rates and availability again if a channel ever falls out of step.

Q: What does overbooking mean?
A: Overbooking is when a hotel accepts more reservations than it can host for the same room and dates, also called a double booking.

Q: Does a channel manager fully prevent overbooking?
A: Real-time two-way sync removes most of the risk; direct bookings that aren't entered and wrong room mappings can still cause problems.

Q: How can hotels avoid overbookings across OTA channels?
A: Connect every OTA to one calendar through a two-way, real-time channel manager instead of updating extranets by hand or relying on calendar (iCal) links. Then make sure every room type is mapped, enter direct bookings immediately and never open rooms directly in an extranet.

Q: What does “walking the guest” mean?
A: Moving a guest who can't be accommodated because of an overbooking to a comparable hotel nearby, usually with the hotel paying the price difference and transport.

# Booking.com Auto-Reply: 12 Free Message Templates (2026)
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/blog/auto-reply-booking-com-messages/

## Booking.com Auto-Reply: 12 Free Message Templates (2026)
By the Hostlio Pro product team , the people who build Hostlio Pro. Published September 21, 2026 , updated September 23, 2026

Short answer: There are three ways to automate Booking.com messages: saved message templates in the extranet, scheduled messages tied to the booking stage, and an AI assistant that understands the guest's question and answers from your hotel information. Templates suit standard information; an AI assistant suits the questions that differ for every guest. Below you'll find 12 free reply templates you can copy straight into the extranet.

Contents

- 1. Message templates
- 2. Scheduled messages
- 3. An AI assistant
- Why response time matters
- 12 free Booking.com reply templates to copy
- How it works in Hostlio Pro

## 1. Message templates

Save frequent answers like check-in time, directions and parking as templates and send them in one click. They're simple, but someone still has to read the message and pick the right template.

## 2. Scheduled messages

Messages sent automatically after booking, a day before arrival or on departure day. Guests are informed before they ask, but these don't answer questions guests write later.

## 3. An AI assistant

It reads the guest's message and writes a reply from your knowledge base in the guest's language. It works best for night-time, multilingual and off-template questions, and it should hand decisions (discounts, complaints) to staff.

Method Works best for Limit

Templates Standard information Someone must read and choose

Scheduled messages Pre-arrival information Doesn't answer incoming questions

AI assistant Questions at any hour, in any language Needs a good knowledge base

## Why response time matters

A fast answer before booking makes the guest's decision easier; a fast answer during the stay shapes satisfaction and reviews.

## 12 free Booking.com reply templates to copy
Save each one as a message template in the Booking.com extranet inbox, replace the parts in [brackets] with your hotel's details, and keep replies short and specific.

## 1. Booking confirmation and thank-you
Dear [Guest name], thank you for booking with [hotel name]. We have received your reservation for [dates] and look forward to welcoming you. If you have any questions before your stay, just reply to this message.
Copy

## 2. Pre-arrival information
Dear [Guest name], we look forward to seeing you on [date]. Our address is [address], and the easiest way to reach us is [directions]. Could you let us know your approximate arrival time so we can be ready for you?
Copy

## 3. Check-in time and early check-in
Dear [Guest name], check-in starts at [14:00]. If you arrive earlier, we will do our best to have your room ready as soon as possible, depending on occupancy that day, and you are welcome to leave your luggage with us in the meantime. Please let us know your expected arrival time.
Copy

## 4. Late check-out request
Dear [Guest name], our standard check-out time is [11:00]. Depending on occupancy, a late check-out until [time] may be possible, and we will confirm it the day before your departure. If it is available, the fee is [price].
Copy

## 5. Late or after-hours arrival
Dear [Guest name], thank you for letting us know. Our reception is open until [time]; for later arrivals, [describe late check-in: night staff, key box or door code sent on the day]. Please send us your estimated arrival time so we can have everything ready.
Copy

## 6. Parking
Dear [Guest name], we have [on-site / nearby] parking at [address]. It costs [price] per day, and spaces are [subject to availability / bookable in advance]. If you are coming by car, let us know and we will note it on your booking.
Copy

## 7. Airport transfer request
Dear [Guest name], we would be happy to arrange a transfer from [airport] to the hotel. The cost is [price] for [number] people. Please send us your flight number and arrival time, and we will confirm the transfer with you.
Copy

## 8. Breakfast
Dear [Guest name], breakfast is served from [07:00] to [10:30] in [location]. Your Booking.com confirmation shows whether breakfast is included in your rate. If it isn't, you can add it at the hotel for [price] per person per day.
Copy

## 9. Luggage storage
Dear [Guest name], of course, you are welcome to leave your luggage with us before check-in or after check-out [free of charge]. Just ask at reception and we will store it safely for you.
Copy

## 10. Pets
Dear [Guest name], thank you for asking in advance. Pets [are / are not] allowed at our property, as stated in the house rules on our Booking.com page. Where pets are allowed, a fee of [price] per night applies; could you tell us the type and size of your pet so we can prepare a suitable room?
Copy

## 11. Invoice request
Dear [Guest name], we will be happy to issue an invoice for your stay. Please send us the company name, tax ID and full billing address, and we will have the invoice ready [at check-out / by email after your stay].
Copy

## 12. Date change or cancellation
Dear [Guest name], the conditions for changes and cancellations depend on the policy of your booking, which you can find in your Booking.com confirmation. You can request a date change or cancellation directly in the Booking.com app or under 'Manage booking'. If you send us your new dates, we will gladly check availability for you.
Copy

Keep payments inside Booking.com: don't send payment links or personal contact details in messages, and make sure your templates match the house rules and policies on your listing.

## How it works in Hostlio Pro

On Pro and Growth, OTA messages including Booking.com land in the inbox of Lio, the AI assistant . Lio answers with your hotel information in the guest's language and leaves what it isn't sure about to you.

Q: Can you auto-reply to Booking.com messages?
A: Yes. Extranet templates and scheduled messages are Booking.com's own tools; question-specific automatic replies need an AI assistant that reads messages.

Q: Can an AI assistant give wrong information?
A: The risk is low when the assistant only uses information the hotel provides and hands uncertain questions to staff.

Q: Where do I save reply templates in Booking.com?
A: In the Booking.com extranet, open the guest messages inbox and save each text as a message template. When you reply, pick the template and fill in the parts in brackets before sending.

# Privacy Policy | Hostlio Pro
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/privacy/

## Privacy Policy
Last updated: October 4, 2026 , Loti Members LLC, 2108 N ST STE N, Sacramento, CA 95816

This Privacy Policy explains how Hostlio Pro, operated by Loti Members LLC (“we”, “us”), collects, uses and shares personal data when you visit hostliopro.com, sign up, or use the Hostlio Pro dashboard, mobile app and guest-facing features.

## 1. Our role
For data about our customers (hotel owners and staff) and website visitors, we are the controller . For data about a hotel’s guests that we process to run the service for that hotel, the hotel is the controller and we act as its processor (a “service provider” under California law). That processing is governed by our Data Processing Addendum . Guests who want to exercise their rights should contact the hotel; we help the hotel respond.

## 2. Data we collect

- Account data: name, email, phone, hotel name, number of rooms, country, guest currency and time zone
- Billing data: plan, billing period and payment status. Card details are collected and stored by Stripe, never by us
- Hotel data: room types, rooms, rates, availability, reservations and settings
- Guest data processed for hotels: guest names, contact details, booking details and the content of guest messages received on WhatsApp and OTA inboxes
- Online check-in data: identity document details (name, document number or, for Turkish ID cards, the T.C. identity number, nationality, date of birth and expiry date), companions and a digital signature, when the hotel uses online check-in. The document’s machine-readable zone is read on the guest’s or the hotel staff’s own device; we do not collect or store images of identity documents. We treat this data as sensitive
- Signup and security data: IP address, a hashed email and the outcome of signup attempts, used to prevent fraud and abuse
- Marketing source: only if you arrive through a link with campaign parameters (UTM parameters or an ad click ID): those parameters, the landing page and the time of your first visit, stored in your browser and sent to us only with your signup or contact form
- Usage data: how the dashboard and app are used, technical logs and, when you use the mobile app, your device’s push notification token

## 3. How we use data

- To provide the service: syncing channels, showing reservations, sending guest messages and running online check-in
- To draft and send AI replies to guest messages on the hotel’s behalf
- To run your subscription: the free trial, automatic charges when the trial ends and at each renewal, invoices and plan limits such as the monthly AI message quota
- To keep the service secure and prevent fraud
- To measure which marketing channels bring customers
- To answer support requests and send service and billing emails
- To meet legal obligations
We do not sell personal data and we do not share it for cross-context behavioural advertising. Guest message content is not used for our marketing. Our AI provider processes message content only to generate replies and, under its commercial terms, does not use it to train its models.

## 4. Legal bases (EEA, UK, Türkiye)
We rely on performance of our contract with you, our legitimate interests (security, fraud prevention, improving the service, measuring marketing), compliance with legal obligations and, where required, your consent. For guest data, the hotel determines the legal basis.

## 5. Who we share data with
We use the subprocessors below. Each is bound by a contract that protects the data. When you connect a sales channel (such as Booking.com, Airbnb or Expedia), data is exchanged with that channel under its own terms.

## 6. International transfers
We are based in the United States and some subprocessors process data outside the EEA, the UK and Türkiye. Where required, transfers are protected by the European Commission’s Standard Contractual Clauses, the UK Addendum or other lawful transfer mechanisms.

## 7. How long we keep data

- Guest message content is anonymised after the retention period the hotel sets in its settings (default: 60 days)
- Guest contact details are kept for 90 days after departure, unless the hotel deletes them sooner
- Online check-in data is kept only as long as the hotel needs it to meet its guest-registration duties, and is deleted with the hotel’s account at the latest
- Account and hotel data are kept while the account is active and deleted within 30 days of a verified deletion request
- Billing records are kept for as long as tax and accounting law requires
- Signup and security logs are kept for a limited period for fraud prevention

## 8. Security
Data is encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. Access is restricted by role and by hotel. Our database provider is SOC 2 Type 2 audited and card payments are handled by Stripe, a PCI DSS Level 1 service provider. More on our Security and data page.

## 9. Your rights

EEA and UK: you can request access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability, and object to processing. You may also complain to your local data protection authority.

California (CCPA/CPRA): you can ask to know, delete and correct your personal information. We do not sell or share personal information, and we will not discriminate against you for exercising your rights.

Türkiye (KVKK): under Article 11 of Law No. 6698 you can learn whether your data is processed, request information, correction or deletion, and object to results arising from automated processing.

To exercise any right, email hello@hostliopro.com . To close your account, see Delete your account .

## 10. Cookies and browser storage
The dashboard uses essential cookies and storage to keep you signed in. Our website stores your language choice in your browser’s local storage. For marketing measurement nothing is stored on ordinary visits: only when you arrive through a link that carries campaign parameters (utm_source, utm_medium, utm_campaign, utm_term, utm_content, or an ad click ID: gclid, msclkid, ttclid, fbclid) does the site save those parameters, the landing page path and the time of that first visit in local storage under the key hostlio_acq . No cookie is set for this. The referring website’s domain is read only for the current page view and is not stored. This record is first-party: the site never shares it with ad networks, it is sent to us only if you submit the signup or contact form (attached to that submission), and it is deleted automatically after 90 days. We rely on our legitimate interest in measuring which marketing channels bring customers; you can object and erase the record at any time by clearing the site data for hostliopro.com in your browser. We do not use advertising cookies.

## Website analytics (Google Analytics 4) — only with your consent
If you choose “Accept” in the cookie banner, we use Google Analytics 4 (provided by Google LLC) to understand how our website is used and to improve it. It records pages viewed, the referring website, device and browser type, approximate location (country/city) and interactions such as clicks on signup buttons, signup form steps, contact form submissions and the monthly/annual price switch. We never send names, email addresses, phone numbers, hotel names or other form contents to Google.
Google Analytics then sets first-party cookies ( _ga , _ga_<ID> ) that expire after up to 2 years. Google Analytics 4 does not log or store IP addresses; Google uses the IP address only briefly to derive the approximate location and then discards it. We keep analytics event data for 14 months, have switched off Google signals and ad personalisation, and do not use this data for advertising.
Google acts as our processor under its data processing terms. Data may be processed in the United States; Google LLC is certified under the EU–US Data Privacy Framework, and Standard Contractual Clauses also apply. Legal basis: your consent (GDPR Art. 6(1)(a); for Türkiye, your explicit consent under KVKK, including for the transfer abroad). Without your consent Google Analytics is not loaded and no request is sent to Google.
Your choice is saved for 6 months in your browser’s local storage under the key hostlio_consent (no cookie). You can withdraw or change it at any time with “Cookie preferences” at the bottom of every page or the button below; withdrawing deletes the Google Analytics cookies.
Cookie preferences

# The Complete Guide to AI Front Desk for Independent Hotels
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/blog/hotel-ai-front-desk-guide/

## The Complete Guide to AI Front Desk for Independent Hotels
By the Hostlio Pro product team , the people who build Hostlio Pro. Published May 1, 2026 , updated September 23, 2026

Contents

- What an AI Front Desk Actually Does
- What AI Cannot Do (Yet)
- The Multilingual Advantage
- How to Set Up an AI Front Desk: Step by Step
- Frequently Asked Questions from Hotel Owners
- The Right Expectation to Set The phrase "AI front desk" can conjure images of robot receptionists and sci-fi lobbies. The reality in 2026 is far more practical — and far more accessible. An AI front desk for an independent hotel is not a physical machine; it's a software layer that handles the routine communication work your front desk currently does manually, around the clock, in any language, without getting tired or going on holiday.

For a small hotel with limited staff, this is not a luxury. It's becoming an operational necessity. Here's everything you need to know about what AI front-desk tools actually do, how to set one up, and what realistic results to expect.

## What an AI Front Desk Actually Does

The core function is simple: when a guest sends a message — via WhatsApp, email, Booking.com inbox, or Airbnb messages — the AI reads it, understands the intent, and sends a helpful, accurate reply without any human involvement. The guest gets an answer within seconds. Your team gets notified only when a message requires human judgement.

In practice, this covers a surprisingly large share of all guest communication. Research across hospitality platforms consistently finds that 70–80% of incoming guest messages fall into predictable categories:

- Check-in and check-out times

- Directions and parking

- WiFi password and room amenities

- Breakfast availability and hours

- Late check-out or early check-in requests

- Local recommendations (restaurants, transport, attractions)

- Booking modifications and cancellation policy questions

- Pre-arrival confirmation and document requests

All of these can be handled by a well-configured AI system with access to your hotel's information — without any human needing to touch the conversation. Beyond reactive replies, an AI front desk also sends proactive messages: booking confirmations, pre-arrival reminders, check-in instructions, and post-stay review requests, all timed automatically based on the booking data.

## What AI Cannot Do (Yet)

Being clear about limitations is important. AI messaging handles language and routine logic well, but it is not equipped to:

- Handle genuinely novel or complex complaints requiring empathy and judgment

- Process payment disputes or chargebacks

- Make real-time decisions about room availability that haven't been configured in advance

- Replace the human connection guests value in a boutique hotel experience

The right mental model is: AI handles the volume so your team can focus on the moments that actually require human presence. A guest messaging at midnight about breakfast hours doesn't need a human; a guest who has just discovered a leak in their bathroom ceiling does.

An AI front desk doesn't replace your staff — it handles the 70% of messages that didn't need human input in the first place, so your team can focus on the 30% that do.

## The Multilingual Advantage

For hotels in international destinations, the language capability of AI messaging is one of its most transformative features. A 15-room hotel in Lisbon might receive messages in English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, and Brazilian Portuguese in the same week. Hiring staff fluent in all of these is impossible at that scale. An AI that responds fluently in the guest's own language — detecting it automatically from the message — is a genuine competitive advantage.

Hostlio Pro handles guest messaging in over 20 languages. When a German-speaking guest writes a question in German, they receive a German reply. When a Japanese traveller asks about transportation from the airport in Japanese, they get a clear, accurate answer in Japanese. Your team sees the conversation in both languages, can review the AI's response, and can intervene if needed — but most of the time, they won't need to.

## How to Set Up an AI Front Desk: Step by Step

-

Connect your booking channels
The AI needs to know about reservations to send timely, accurate messages. Connect your OTA channels (Booking.com, Airbnb, Expedia, etc.) so the system has real-time access to guest names, arrival dates, room types, and special requests.

-

Build your hotel's knowledge base
Configure the information the AI uses to answer questions: check-in/check-out times, breakfast hours and included items, parking instructions, WiFi details, amenities, cancellation policy, and a list of local recommendations. The more complete this is, the fewer escalations you'll see.

-

Set up your message sequences
Define the proactive messages the AI sends automatically: a booking confirmation within minutes of reservation, a pre-arrival message 48 hours out, check-in instructions on the day of arrival, a mid-stay check-in (optional), and a post-stay review request. Customise the tone to match your hotel's personality.

-

Connect WhatsApp Business API
WhatsApp is the primary channel for AI messaging. You'll need a WhatsApp Business API number — which Hostlio Pro provides as part of the setup — linked to a dedicated phone number for your property.

-

Test with real conversations
Before going live, send test messages covering common scenarios. Check that the AI's replies are accurate, appropriately toned, and correctly localised. Adjust the knowledge base based on any gaps you find.

-

Set escalation rules
Define which types of messages should immediately alert your team — complaints, urgent requests, messages the AI cannot confidently answer. Most platforms let you set keywords or confidence thresholds that trigger a human handoff notification.

## Frequently Asked Questions from Hotel Owners

Will guests know they're talking to an AI?
With Hostlio Pro you can choose: the AI can identify itself as an automated assistant, or communicate in your hotel's name without specifying. Most guests care more about getting a fast, accurate answer than about who — or what — sent it. Response time matters more than disclosure.

What happens if the AI gives a wrong answer?
All AI responses are logged and visible to your team in the dashboard. If you notice an incorrect reply, you can correct the knowledge base to prevent it recurring. For sensitive topics — pricing disputes, allergy information — it's worth reviewing AI responses more closely in the first few weeks.

How long does setup take?
Most independent hotels are fully operational within a day or two. The majority of setup time goes into building the knowledge base — which is simply documenting things you already know about your property. Hostlio Pro's onboarding walks you through every step.

What's the ROI?
For a hotel handling 20 bookings per month, an AI front desk typically saves 8–15 hours of staff time monthly in message handling alone. At any reasonable staff cost, that's a positive return within the first month. The secondary benefit — faster response times leading to higher review scores — compounds over time.

## The Right Expectation to Set

An AI front desk will not make your hotel feel robotic or impersonal — if set up correctly, it will make it feel more responsive and attentive than ever before. Guests who message at 11 PM and receive a friendly, accurate reply within 30 seconds leave better reviews than guests who wait until the next morning for an email response. The technology enables the experience; your hotel's character and hospitality fill in everything that matters.

The independent hotels that are winning in 2026 are the ones that combine genuine human warmth with operational tools sharp enough to handle the volume. An AI front desk is one of the highest-leverage tools available for achieving exactly that balance.

# 5 Ways to Reduce No-Shows at Your Independent Hotel
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/blog/how-to-reduce-hotel-no-shows/

## 5 Ways to Reduce No-Shows at Your Independent Hotel
By the Hostlio Pro product team , the people who build Hostlio Pro. Published May 1, 2026 , updated September 23, 2026

Contents

- 1. Require a Non-Refundable Deposit at Booking
- 2. Send Automated Pre-Arrival Reminders
- 3. Make Cancellation Easy — So Guests Use It
- 4. Implement a Credit Card Guarantee Policy
- 5. Build a Last-Minute Rebooking Workflow
- The Bottom Line A guest who books a room and never arrives is one of the most frustrating — and expensive — problems an independent hotel faces. Unlike a large chain with dozens of rooms to fill at short notice, a 20-room boutique property loses a significant percentage of nightly revenue every time a no-show occurs. Industry data suggests that no-shows cost the hospitality sector billions globally each year, with independent hotels often absorbing the highest per-room losses because they lack the scale to quickly rebook.

The good news: no-show rates are largely preventable. With the right policies and tools in place, most properties can cut their no-show rate by 40–60%. Here are five strategies that work.

## 1. Require a Non-Refundable Deposit at Booking

The single most effective deterrent to no-shows is a financial stake. When a guest has already paid 20–30% of the room rate upfront, they are far less likely to simply not show up. If their plans change, they are more likely to contact you to reschedule rather than walk away from paid money.

Many independent hoteliers worry that a deposit requirement will reduce bookings. In practice, the conversion rate impact is minimal for leisure travellers with genuine intent — and it filters out the window-shoppers who book three properties and keep only one. The net revenue effect is almost always positive.

On OTA channels like Booking.com and Airbnb, you can configure deposit or non-refundable rate plans directly in the extranet. For direct bookings, payment processors like Stripe make it straightforward to collect a partial payment at reservation time.

## 2. Send Automated Pre-Arrival Reminders

A surprising number of no-shows are not intentional — guests simply forget, misread their dates, or assume a booking can be silently abandoned. A sequence of friendly automated messages dramatically reduces these accidental no-shows.

A simple reminder schedule that works well:

- 7 days before arrival: A warm confirmation message with check-in time, address, and parking details.

- 48 hours before arrival: A shorter "we're looking forward to welcoming you" message with a link to the cancellation policy.

- Day of arrival: A quick "your room is ready" message with check-in instructions.

Tools like Hostlio Pro can automate guest messaging on WhatsApp and in your OTA inboxes, so you don't need to send each message manually. At an average open rate of over 90% for WhatsApp, these reminders actually get read.

## 3. Make Cancellation Easy — So Guests Use It

This sounds counterintuitive, but hotels with frictionless cancellation processes experience fewer no-shows. When a guest knows it is easy to cancel, they are more likely to do so rather than avoid the conversation altogether. A cancelled room at 72 hours notice is far more valuable than a no-show: you have time to rebook it.

A cancelled room you can rebook is worth more than a no-show where you earn the deposit but lose the chance to sell the room again.

Include a clear, one-click cancellation link in your confirmation emails. Make your cancellation policy visible and written in plain language. Guests who feel they are being treated fairly are loyal guests.

## 4. Implement a Credit Card Guarantee Policy

For rooms without a deposit, requiring a credit card guarantee — where you charge the full amount if the guest no-shows — is the next best deterrent. This is standard practice at chain hotels and is increasingly accepted by independent travellers.

The key is transparency: display the guarantee policy clearly at the point of booking. Most OTAs support guarantee policies at the rate plan level, and guests who see the policy tend to either book with genuine intent or choose a refundable rate where they know they are covered. Either outcome is better than a silent no-show.

## 5. Build a Last-Minute Rebooking Workflow

Even with the best preventive measures, some no-shows will still occur. Having a rapid rebooking workflow in place limits the revenue impact. This means: listing last-minute availability on platforms that specialise in same-day bookings, having a WhatsApp broadcast list of previous guests you can message with a special rate, and training front-desk staff to upsell walk-ins.

Hostlio Pro's room rack calendar shows real-time availability across all OTAs in one place, so when a no-show happens, you can immediately see what's available, adjust pricing, and activate a last-minute promotion — all from a single screen without logging into four different extranets.

## The Bottom Line

No-shows are not an inevitable cost of running a hotel. They are a symptom of weak policies, poor communication, and fragmented tools. By combining a clear deposit or guarantee policy with automated WhatsApp reminders and a centralised availability view, most independent hotels can reduce their no-show rate to under 3% — and protect thousands in revenue every month.

# Independent Hotels vs. Chains: Competing with Tech in 2026
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/blog/independent-hotel-vs-chain-technology/

## Independent Hotels vs. Chains: Competing with Tech in 2026
By the Hostlio Pro product team , the people who build Hostlio Pro. Published May 1, 2026 , updated September 23, 2026

Contents

- What Chains Had That You Didn't — Until Now
- Where Independent Hotels Have the Natural Edge
- The Three Technology Priorities That Matter Most
- The Loyalty Programme Question
- The Cost of Doing Nothing For decades, the technology gap between independent hotels and large chains felt insurmountable. Marriott, Hilton, and IHG had entire departments dedicated to building and maintaining proprietary property management systems, loyalty platforms, and guest-facing apps — investments worth hundreds of millions of dollars that a 25-room boutique hotel could never replicate.

That gap has closed faster than most people in the industry realise. The SaaS revolution in hospitality technology means that independent hotels can now access the same capabilities — AI-driven guest messaging, real-time channel management across 10+ OTAs, automated visa and registration forms, dynamic pricing tools — at a fraction of the cost, with no technical team required.

This is not a small shift. It fundamentally changes the competitive landscape for independent accommodation. Here's where the playing field has levelled, and where you still have natural advantages chains cannot buy.

## What Chains Had That You Didn't — Until Now

Five years ago, accessing even two or three of these capabilities as an independent hotel required cobbling together expensive, incompatible tools from different vendors, each requiring separate logins, contracts, and maintenance. Today, platforms like Hostlio Pro bring all of them into a single dashboard at a price point that makes sense for a property with 10 rooms.

## Where Independent Hotels Have the Natural Edge

Technology parity is only part of the story. The independent hotel's deepest competitive advantage has never been technology — it's been authenticity, flexibility, and human connection. These are things chains actively struggle to replicate at scale.

- Personal character: A family-run riad in Marrakech, a boutique hotel overlooking the Amalfi Coast, a converted farmhouse in Tuscany — these properties have a story and a personality that a Marriott Courtyard simply cannot match. Guests who choose independent hotels are often actively seeking something a chain cannot offer.

- Decision speed: An independent owner can decide to add a late-checkout policy, change a cancellation window, or create a custom package for a corporate client in minutes. A chain property requires approvals through multiple layers of corporate hierarchy.

- Local knowledge: Independent hoteliers are embedded in their communities in ways that chain GMs — often rotated every 18–24 months — are not. Recommendations for the best local restaurant, the quieter beach, the unmarked hiking trail: guests value this deeply and review it explicitly.

- Pricing agility: Without a corporate rate card to adhere to, independent hotels can respond to demand signals instantly — dropping prices during a slow period or capturing premium rates during a local festival that a chain's pricing system hasn't flagged.

## The Three Technology Priorities That Matter Most

Given limited budgets and management time, independent hotels should focus their technology investment on the three areas with the highest ROI:

1. Channel management with real-time sync. Being on more OTAs — Booking.com, Airbnb, Expedia, Agoda, Google Hotels — dramatically increases visibility and bookings. But listing on multiple channels without real-time sync creates double-booking risk. A channel manager that syncs in seconds, not minutes, is the foundation everything else rests on.

2. Automated guest communication. The biggest operational cost for most small hotels is the time spent answering repetitive guest messages: directions, breakfast hours, parking, check-in instructions. AI-powered messaging via WhatsApp can handle 70–80% of these automatically, in the guest's language, without any staff involvement. This time saving translates directly into cost reduction or reallocation to higher-value tasks.

3. A visual room rack. Having a single, accurate picture of all reservations — regardless of which channel they came from — eliminates the manual reconciliation that leads to errors, double bookings, and missed opportunities to upsell adjacent rooms.

You don't need to compete with chain hotels on brand scale. You need to match them on operational efficiency — then beat them on personality. Technology enables the first; you bring the second.

## The Loyalty Programme Question

One area where chains still hold a meaningful advantage is loyalty programmes. Marriott Bonvoy and Hilton Honors drive significant repeat bookings from members who choose the brand specifically to accumulate points. Independent hotels cannot replicate this at scale on their own.

The practical response is two-fold: first, build direct relationships through WhatsApp and email that make guests want to return regardless of points; second, consider listing on platforms like Google Hotels, which now drives significant direct-booking intent from guests who are not loyal to any particular chain. Independent hotels that rank well in Google's local search results capture a growing segment of travellers who prioritise location and reviews over brand loyalty.

## The Cost of Doing Nothing

The risk of inaction is real. As more independent hotels adopt channel management, AI messaging, and real-time room management tools, the guests they attract will increasingly expect fast responses, seamless booking experiences, and digital communication. Hotels that still rely on manual processes and email-only communication will feel the gap not just in efficiency — but in review scores, which directly affect OTA ranking and future bookings.

The good news is that the cost of adoption has never been lower. Hostlio Pro offers the full suite of channel management, AI messaging, and room management starting at $39 per month — less than the cost of a single slow night's lost revenue. The technology gap between independent hotels and chains no longer requires millions to close. It requires the right tools and the will to use them.

This Data Processing Addendum (“DPA”) forms part of the Terms of Service between Loti Members LLC, operator of Hostlio Pro (“Processor”, “we”), and the customer that has accepted them (“Controller”, “you”). It applies to personal data of your guests and staff that we process on your behalf when providing Hostlio Pro (“Customer Personal Data”). It takes effect when you accept the Terms of Service. ## 1. Definitions
“Data Protection Law” means all laws that apply to the processing of Customer Personal Data, including the EU General Data Protection Regulation 2016/679 (“GDPR”), the UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018, Turkish Law No. 6698 on the Protection of Personal Data (“KVKK”), Brazil’s LGPD and the California Consumer Privacy Act as amended (“CCPA”). “Controller”, “processor”, “data subject”, “personal data breach” and “processing” have the meanings given in the GDPR. “Subprocessor” means a third party we engage to process Customer Personal Data.

## 2. Roles and instructions
You are the controller and we are the processor (and, under the CCPA, your service provider). We process Customer Personal Data only on your documented instructions, which are these Terms, this DPA and your use and configuration of Hostlio Pro, unless the law requires otherwise; in that case we will inform you first unless the law prohibits it. We will tell you if we believe an instruction infringes Data Protection Law. You are responsible for the lawfulness of the processing, including informing guests and having a legal basis.

## 3. Confidentiality
Everyone we authorise to process Customer Personal Data is bound by confidentiality obligations.

## 4. Security

## 5. Subprocessors
You give general authorisation for us to use subprocessors. The current list is in Annex 3 and on our Security and data page. We will notify you by email or in the dashboard at least 30 days before adding or replacing a subprocessor; you may object on reasonable data-protection grounds, and if we cannot resolve the objection you may terminate the affected service and receive a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees for it. We impose data-protection obligations on each subprocessor that are no less protective than this DPA and remain responsible for their performance.

## 6. Data subject requests

## 7. Personal data breaches
We will notify you without undue delay, and in any case within 48 hours, after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting Customer Personal Data. The notice will describe the breach, the data and data subjects concerned, likely consequences and the measures taken, as far as that information is available.

## 8. Assistance
We give reasonable assistance with data protection impact assessments and prior consultations with supervisory authorities, taking into account the information available to us.

## 9. Deletion and return
You can export your data while your account is active. After the account ends we delete Customer Personal Data within 30 days, except where the law requires us to keep it. Guest message content is anonymised after the retention period you configure (default 60 days).

## 10. Audits
We make available the information reasonably necessary to demonstrate compliance with this DPA, including our subprocessors’ security reports where they allow it. If that is not sufficient, you may carry out an audit once a year, with 30 days’ notice, during business hours, at your cost and under confidentiality.

## 11. International transfers
Where Customer Personal Data is transferred from the EEA, Switzerland, the UK or Türkiye to a country without an adequacy decision, the parties agree that the Standard Contractual Clauses adopted by Commission Implementing Decision (EU) 2021/914 (Module 2, controller to processor) are incorporated by reference, with the UK International Data Transfer Addendum and the standard contracts published under KVKK Article 9 where applicable. ## 12. CCPA

## 13. Liability and precedence
Each party’s liability under this DPA is subject to the limitations in the Terms of Service, except where Data Protection Law does not allow this. If this DPA conflicts with the Terms, this DPA prevails for the processing of Customer Personal Data; the Standard Contractual Clauses prevail over both.

# RevPAR, ADR & Occupancy Rate Calculator (Free) | Hostlio Pro
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/tools/revpar-adr-occupancy-calculator/

## RevPAR, ADR and occupancy calculator
Enter your rooms, the room nights you sold and your room revenue for the period. Occupancy rate, average daily rate (ADR) and revenue per available room (RevPAR) update instantly.

Currency USD EUR GBP TRY BRL Rooms available to sell Days in the period Room nights sold Each occupied room counts once per night. A guest staying 3 nights = 3 room nights. Room revenue for the period Room revenue only; leave out extras such as transfers, tours and taxes (whatever you choose, be consistent).
Available room nights –
Occupancy rate –
ADR (average daily rate) –
RevPAR (revenue per available room) –

Calculated in your browser; your numbers are never sent anywhere.

## The formulas

## Occupancy rate
Room nights sold ÷ available room nights × 100
The share of your rooms that were occupied. Available room nights = rooms × days.

## ADR (average daily rate)
Room revenue ÷ room nights sold
The average price of one room night sold. It ignores empty rooms.

## RevPAR (revenue per available room)
Room revenue ÷ available room nights = ADR × occupancy rate
Combines price and occupancy in one number, so it also shows the cost of empty rooms.

## A worked example
A 12-room boutique hotel sold 285 room nights in a 31-day month and earned $39,900 in room revenue:

- Available room nights: 12 × 31 = 372
- Occupancy rate: 285 ÷ 372 = 76.6%
- ADR: $39,900 ÷ 285 = $140
- RevPAR: $39,900 ÷ 372 = $107.26 (or $140 × 76.6%) The calculator's default values are this example; replace them with your own numbers.

## What each number tells you

## High occupancy, low RevPAR
You may be selling rooms too cheaply. Raising rates a little on busy dates can lift RevPAR without losing much occupancy.

## High ADR, low occupancy
Your rate may be above demand, or your distribution may be thin. Appearing on more channels and reviewing minimum-stay rules can help.

## Comparing RevPAR
Compare the same period last year, or properties of a similar size. For hotels with different room counts RevPAR is fairer than total revenue.

## Common mistakes

- Adding breakfast, transfer and tour income to room revenue (it inflates ADR and RevPAR).
- Removing out-of-order rooms from available rooms one month but not the next. Pick one method and keep it.
- Counting complimentary rooms as sold with no revenue, which drags ADR down.
- Mixing gross and net revenue for commission-based channels. For channel profitability use the OTA commission calculator .

## In Hostlio Pro these numbers come in by themselves
The Analytics screen in the Hostlio Pro dashboard calculates occupancy, ADR and RevPAR from your reservations, compares them with the previous period and last year, and shows gross revenue, commission and net revenue per channel. You can export reports to Excel. See all features or compare plans (from $49 a month).

Q: How do you calculate RevPAR?
A: Divide room revenue for the period by available room nights. You get the same result by multiplying ADR by the occupancy rate: a $140 ADR at 76.6% occupancy is about $107 RevPAR.

Q: What is the difference between ADR and RevPAR?
A: ADR is the average price of the rooms you sold; RevPAR also counts the rooms you didn't sell. That's why RevPAR shows price and occupancy performance in one number.

Q: How do you calculate hotel occupancy rate?
A: Divide room nights sold by available room nights (rooms × days) and multiply by 100. A 20-room hotel that sold 450 room nights in 30 days has 450 ÷ 600 = 75% occupancy.

Q: Should breakfast be included in room revenue?
A: Separating breakfast included in a package rate is often impractical; what matters is using the same method every period. Extras sold separately (transfers, tours, paid breakfast) are not room revenue.

Q: Are the numbers I enter saved?
A: No. The calculation runs entirely in your browser; nothing is sent to a server.

## How it's calculated

- Commission = gross amount × commission rate
- Other fees = gross amount × fee rate (e.g. virtual card or payment processing fees)
- Net revenue = gross amount − commission − other fees
- Net per night = net revenue ÷ nights

## Example
A 3-night booking worth $1,200 with 18% commission and a 1.5% payment fee: commission $216, other fees $18, net revenue $966, net per night $322. Of the $400 the guest pays per night, you keep $322.
Some channels charge commission on the amount including taxes, others on the amount excluding taxes. Enter the gross amount on the basis your contract uses. This page is not tax advice.

## Compare with a direct booking
When the same room is sold direct (phone, WhatsApp, your website) there is no commission. If you keep 80.5%, as in the example, you could offer up to 19.5% off on a direct booking and still not earn less than from the OTA sale. Remember direct sales have their own costs (payment processing, advertising).

The Analytics screen in Hostlio Pro shows gross revenue, commission and net revenue side by side for every channel, so you can see which one really pays after commission. The channel manager keeps 100+ OTAs on one calendar, and Lio answers WhatsApp questions so you can take direct booking requests. Plans start at $49 a month.

RevPAR, ADR and occupancy calculator · AI messaging ROI calculator

Q: How do you calculate OTA commission?
A: Multiply the booking amount by the rate in your contract: $1,200 × 18% = $216. For net revenue, subtract that and any payment fees from the gross amount.

Q: Is commission charged on the amount including taxes?
A: It depends on the channel and country. Your contract and the channel's monthly invoice state which amount is used; enter that amount in the calculator.

Q: What is net ADR?
A: The average revenue left per room night sold after commission and fees. When comparing channels, net ADR gives a truer picture than gross ADR.

Q: Are my numbers saved?
A: No. The calculation runs in your browser and nothing is sent anywhere.

## Which one fits you?

- Under 10 rooms, owner-run: look for a flat fee with the channel manager included and a mobile app. Booking-fee models look cheap until high season.

- 10–50 rooms with a small team: prioritise one inbox for guest messages, staff roles and reliable OTA sync. Compare the full yearly cost, including add-ons.

- Many outlets (restaurant, spa) or complex groups: broader platforms with POS and payments may be worth the quote process.

# PMS vs channel manager: what's the difference?
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/blog/pms-vs-channel-manager/

## PMS vs channel manager: what's the difference?
By the Hostlio Pro product team , the people who build Hostlio Pro. Published October 8, 2026 , updated September 23, 2026

Short answer: A PMS (property management system) runs the inside of your hotel: the reservation calendar, rooms, guests, housekeeping and reports. A channel manager runs the connection to the outside: it sends your availability, rates and restrictions to Booking.com, Airbnb, Expedia and other channels, and brings their bookings back. If you sell on more than one online channel, you need both functions. For a small hotel the simplest setup is usually a PMS with a built-in channel manager, so there is only one calendar and nothing to keep in sync between two systems.

Contents

- What a PMS does
- What a channel manager does
- PMS vs channel manager at a glance
- How the two work together
- Three ways to set it up
- Do you need both?
- What it costs
- Questions to ask before you decide
- How it works in Hostlio Pro
- Sources

## What a PMS does

The PMS is the system your front desk lives in. It is the single record of who is staying, in which room, on which dates and at what price. Typical PMS jobs:

- Reservation calendar (room rack): every booking on a timeline by room, with room moves, date changes and conflict checks.

- Rooms and housekeeping: clean, dirty or out-of-order status and the day's cleaning list.

- Guests: contact details, check-in data, notes and stay history.

- Direct bookings: phone, email, walk-in and repeat guests entered by staff.

- Reports: occupancy, ADR, RevPAR, revenue and cancellations.

## What a channel manager does

A channel manager is a data link between your inventory and the places that sell it. It works in two directions:

- From the hotel to the channels: availability (how many rooms of each type can be sold), rates and restrictions such as minimum stay, closed to arrival, closed to departure and stop sell. The industry calls this ARI: availability, rates and inventory.

- From the channels to the hotel: new bookings, modifications and cancellations.
When the last free room sells on Airbnb, the channel manager receives the booking and sends “0 rooms” for those dates to Booking.com and Expedia, usually within seconds. That is what prevents most double bookings; see our guide on how to prevent overbooking .

## PMS vs channel manager at a glance

PMS Channel manager
Main job Runs daily operations: calendar, rooms, guests, reports Distributes availability and rates to channels and imports their bookings
Who uses it Front desk, housekeeping, management, accounting Mostly runs in the background; set up by the owner or revenue manager
Talks to Your team (and, through integrations, other tools) OTAs, metasearch and other sales channels
Without it Bookings live in spreadsheets, extranets and paper Availability must be updated by hand in every extranet
Key risk if it fails Lost or duplicated reservations, no overview Overbooking and rates that differ between channels

## How the two work together

Think of the PMS as the source of truth and the channel manager as the messenger. A typical flow:

- A guest books a double room on Booking.com for 12–14 May.

- The channel manager receives the reservation and passes it to the PMS, where it appears on the room rack.

- The PMS recalculates availability for double rooms on those dates.

- The channel manager sends the new availability to every other connected channel.

- When you later change a rate or close a date in the PMS, the same path runs in reverse.
The weak points are the hand-offs. If the PMS and the channel manager come from different vendors, they need an interface between them, and every room type and rate plan must be mapped twice: once between the channel and the channel manager, and once between the channel manager and the PMS.

## Three ways to set it up

Setup How it works Good for Watch out for
PMS only, no channel manager You update each OTA extranet by hand One channel, very few rooms Overbooking risk grows with every extra channel
Standalone channel manager + separate PMS Two systems linked by an interface Hotels tied to an existing PMS they want to keep Two bills, two support desks, double mapping, sync gaps between systems
PMS with a built-in channel manager One system, one calendar Most small and independent hotels Check which channels are certified and how fast sync is

## Do you need both?

- You sell only direct and on one OTA: a PMS is enough to start; closing dates by hand in one extranet is manageable.

- You sell on two or more online channels: you need channel manager functionality. Updating several extranets by hand is the most common cause of overbooking at independent hotels.

- You already use a PMS you like: check whether it has its own channel manager or a certified integration with one before adding a second vendor.

- You are choosing from scratch: a PMS with a built-in channel manager avoids the integration layer entirely. Our guide on choosing hotel management software for a small hotel lists the other criteria.

## What it costs

Channel managers are priced in several ways, and some PMS vendors only include one in their higher plans. Two examples from vendors' own pricing pages (8 October 2026):

- Per room and per connection: Beds24 charges a base fee, a fee per room and a fee per room type for each channel connection; its pricing page says “from €15.50” a month.

- Only in a higher plan: Sirvoy offers a free plan for one room and a Starter plan, but the channel manager is listed only in its Pro plan (€79 a month for up to 10 rooms, paid monthly).
Other models charge a percentage of booking revenue or a fee per reservation, which grows in high season. When you compare, add up the PMS, the channel manager and any per-booking fees, then check what each channel really leaves you after commission with our OTA commission calculator .

## Questions to ask before you decide

- Which channels are connected, and are the connections certified by the channels themselves?

- Is sync real-time or on a schedule? What happens if a channel is down?

- Do rates and restrictions (minimum stay, closed to arrival or departure, stop sell) go to every channel, or only availability?

- Do modifications and cancellations come back automatically?

- When a room is out of order, does availability drop on the channels too?

- Who maps room types and rate plans at setup, and is that help included?

- Is the price flat, or does it depend on rooms, channels or bookings?

## How it works in Hostlio Pro

Hostlio Pro is a PMS with the channel manager built in, on every plan. Connections to 100+ channels, including Booking.com, Airbnb, Expedia, Agoda, Trip.com and Google Hotels, run over certified links through Channex, so bookings, modifications and cancellations land on the same room rack you work in. One grid holds price, minimum and maximum stay, closed to arrival, closed to departure and stop sell for every room type and rate plan, and you can enter a whole season by date range. When a room is taken out of order, availability drops on the channels automatically. The analytics show gross revenue, commission and net for each channel.

There is no per-booking fee or revenue percentage: Starter costs $49 a month, Pro $89 and Growth $149, with a 7-day free trial. See pricing for room limits and what each plan includes.

Q: Is a channel manager part of a PMS?
A: Sometimes. Many PMS products include a channel manager, others integrate with a separate one, and some include it only in higher plans. Check the plan details rather than the feature list.

Q: Can I use a channel manager without a PMS?
A: Yes, many standalone channel managers have a basic calendar. You will still need somewhere to manage rooms, guests, housekeeping and reports, which is the job of a PMS.

Q: Does a channel manager stop all overbookings?
A: Real-time two-way sync removes most of the risk. Direct bookings entered late, wrong room mappings and channels that are temporarily unreachable can still cause problems.

Q: Is the channel manager included in every Hostlio Pro plan?
A: Yes. Starter, Pro and Growth all include the channel manager with 100+ channels. There are no per-booking fees.

# WhatsApp for hotels: setup, Meta's rules and AI replies (2026)
URL: https://hostliopro.com/en/blog/whatsapp-hotel-guest-communication/

## WhatsApp for hotels: setup, Meta's rules and AI replies (2026)
By the Hostlio Pro product team , the people who build Hostlio Pro. Published May 1, 2026 , updated September 23, 2026

Short answer: WhatsApp works well for hotels because guests already use it and reply quickly. A small property can start with the free WhatsApp Business app on one phone. Once several people need to answer, or you want automatic replies and a link to your reservations, you need the WhatsApp Business Platform (Meta's Cloud API), usually through your PMS or a messaging provider. Three rules shape everything: guests must opt in, free-form replies are only possible within 24 hours of the guest's last message, and anything you send outside that window must be a template Meta has approved.

Contents

- Why hotels use WhatsApp
- WhatsApp Business app or WhatsApp Business Platform?
- The 24-hour customer service window
- Message templates
- What Meta charges
- Opt-in and opt-out: what the policy requires
- Messaging limits
- Answering in every guest's language
- What an AI assistant can and can't do on WhatsApp
- Setting up WhatsApp for your hotel: a checklist
- How Hostlio Pro's Lio fits in
- Sources

## Why hotels use WhatsApp

For many travellers WhatsApp is the default way to message a business, especially across Europe, Latin America, the Middle East and Türkiye. A question on WhatsApp gets read; an email often doesn't. For a hotel that means fewer phone calls at reception, fewer “we never got your email” moments and an easy channel for the practical questions every stay produces:

- Before arrival: check-in time, parking, directions, early arrival, airport transfer

- During the stay: towels, breakfast hours, a restaurant tip, a late check-out request

- After departure: a forgotten charger, an invoice, a question about the next visit
The catch is staffing. Guests write at 2 a.m., in languages your team doesn't speak, and expect an answer in minutes. That is where setup choices and automation matter.

## WhatsApp Business app or WhatsApp Business Platform?

Meta offers two products. The app is free to download and is designed for small businesses talking to customers from a single device. The Platform is accessed through an API, either directly through the Cloud API that Meta hosts or through a business solution provider, and is built for automation and integration with your other systems.

WhatsApp Business app WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API)
Cost to start Free app No app fee; Meta charges per message (see below)
Who answers Staff on the phone and linked devices Any number of team members through your software
Automation Greeting and away messages, quick replies Full automation, AI replies, integration with your PMS
Messages outside 24 hours Not restricted the same way Only approved templates
Good for A few rooms, one person answering Hotels with a team, several channels or automation needs

Meta's older self-hosted option, the On-Premises API, was retired in October 2025; new integrations use the Cloud API. When you register a number on the Platform, it must be a number you own that can receive a call or SMS for verification, and your display name is reviewed against Meta's guidelines.

## The 24-hour customer service window

This is the rule that surprises most hotels. Whenever a guest messages you, a 24-hour customer service window opens, and it resets each time the guest writes again. Inside the window you can send any normal reply, without approval. Once the window closes, you can only send pre-approved message templates.

In practice: a guest who asked about parking yesterday morning and hasn't written since can't receive a free-form “Your room is ready” message today. Either you use an approved template, or you reach them another way (email, phone, the OTA inbox).

## Message templates

Templates are fixed messages with placeholders, such as a booking confirmation or a check-in reminder, that Meta reviews before you can use them. Each template must be categorised as marketing , utility (related to a specific transaction, like a booking) or authentication (one-time codes). Review is automated and can take up to 24 hours; only approved templates can be sent.

Keep utility templates genuinely transactional. A “Your booking is confirmed” message with a promotion bolted on will be treated as marketing.

## What Meta charges

Since 1 July 2025 the Platform uses per-message pricing instead of the older per-conversation model. Meta's current pricing page states that, from 1 October 2026, it also charges per message for service messages and for utility messages sent in reply to users inside the 24-hour window. Messages sent within a 72-hour free entry point window, which opens when someone starts a chat from a Click-to-WhatsApp ad or a Facebook call-to-action button, remain free. Rates depend on the recipient's country and the message category, so check Meta's rate card and ask your provider how these fees are billed. The free Business app is not affected.

## Opt-in and opt-out: what the policy requires

The WhatsApp Business Messaging Policy allows you to contact people only if they have given you their phone number and have opted in to receive messages from you. You must respect any request to stop, made on WhatsApp or elsewhere. For a hotel this usually means:

- Ask for consent where you collect the number: the booking form, online check-in or at the desk. Say what kind of messages to expect.

- Keep a record of the consent with the reservation.

- Don't add OTA guests to promotional lists just because a phone number came with the booking.

- Answer “stop” requests immediately and remove the number.
When a guest writes to you first, you can reply within the window. The opt-in question matters mostly for messages you start yourself, such as reminders and offers.

## Messaging limits

Messaging limits cap how many different people you can reach with messages you start (outside a customer service window) in a rolling 24 hours. New accounts start at 250 recipients; the next tiers are 2,000, 10,000, 100,000 and unlimited. Since October 2025 the limit applies to your whole Meta business portfolio, shared by all its numbers. Business verification, or sending good-quality templates, moves you up. Replies to guests who wrote to you don't count against this limit, and most small hotels never reach it.

## Answering in every guest's language

A hotel in Lisbon or Antalya can receive messages in a dozen languages in one week. Guests who can write in their own language ask clearer questions and are less likely to misunderstand the answer. Translation tools help, but copying text in and out of a translator at night is exactly the kind of work that slips. An AI assistant that detects the language and answers in it closes that gap, provided your team can still read the conversation in its own language.

## What an AI assistant can and can't do on WhatsApp

Meta's terms bar companies whose main product is a general-purpose AI assistant from using the WhatsApp Business Platform. A hotel using automation to answer its own guests is a different case, and the messaging policy allows automated replies inside the 24-hour window as long as you also offer a prompt, clear way to reach a human: an in-chat handover, a phone number, an email address or the front desk.

A good AI assistant can It shouldn't, or can't
Answer routine questions 24/7 from your own hotel information Invent an answer to something you never told it
Reply in the guest's language Message guests outside the 24-hour window with free text
Collect dates and guests for a booking request and pass it on Confirm a booking, take payment or grant a discount on its own
Recognise complaints, refunds and special requests and hand them over Handle a complaint that needs judgement or compensation
Tell you which questions it couldn't answer Replace the opt-in your guests gave you

Start in approval mode for the first days, read every draft, and switch topics to automatic once the answers are consistent. Our guide on answering hotel guest messages with AI covers that rollout in more detail.

## Setting up WhatsApp for your hotel: a checklist

- Choose the number. A dedicated business number that your team, not one person, controls.

- Decide app or Platform. One person answering a handful of messages: the app may be enough. A team, automation or a PMS link: the Platform.

- Prepare your hotel information. Check-in and check-out times, parking, breakfast, pets, transfers, house rules. Automatic replies are only as good as this.

- Set handover rules. Which topics always go to a person: discounts, refunds, complaints, group requests.

- Add the number where guests look. Confirmation emails, your website, the Google Business Profile, the OTA listing where allowed.

- Collect consent if you plan to send messages first, and keep the record.

- Plan the templates you will need outside the 24-hour window and submit them for review.

## How Hostlio Pro's Lio fits in

In Hostlio Pro you connect your hotel's own WhatsApp number from the dashboard through Meta's official signup flow, on every plan. WhatsApp messages then arrive in one inbox, where Lio, the AI assistant , answers from your hotel information and reservation data in the guest's language. You read Lio's reply translated into your language; messages you write yourself are sent as you wrote them. You choose how much Lio does on its own: fully automatic, automatic for routine questions with drafts for the rest (the default), or drafts only. Discounts, refunds, complaints and booking requests come to you for approval by default.

- Inside the window, by design. Lio replies to guests who write to you. If a guest's 24-hour window has closed, a free-form reply can't be delivered, and the dashboard tells you so you can reach the guest another way. Hostlio Pro doesn't send WhatsApp marketing campaigns.

- Booking requests (Pro and Growth). Lio collects dates, guests and room preference, quotes from your own rates and availability, and sends you the request. It becomes a reservation only when you approve it.

Q: Is WhatsApp Business free for hotels?
A: The WhatsApp Business app is free. The WhatsApp Business Platform (API) has no app fee, but Meta charges per message; from 1 October 2026 that includes service replies inside the 24-hour window, while messages within a 72-hour free entry point window from Click-to-WhatsApp ads stay free. Your software provider may charge separately.

Q: Can a hotel message a guest who hasn't written for days?
A: Only with a message template that Meta has approved, and only if the guest opted in to receive messages from you. Free-form replies are possible only within 24 hours of the guest's last message.

Q: Do I need the WhatsApp Business API for automatic replies?
A: For anything beyond the app's greeting, away messages and quick replies, yes. AI replies and integration with a PMS run on the WhatsApp Business Platform.

Q: Is an AI chatbot allowed on WhatsApp?
A: Meta's terms prohibit companies whose primary product is a general-purpose AI assistant from using the Platform. Businesses may automate replies to their own customers inside the 24-hour window, as long as they offer a clear way to reach a human.

Q: Can Lio send WhatsApp reminders before arrival?
A: Not today. Lio answers guests who write to you, within WhatsApp's 24-hour window. The online check-in link can be sent automatically by email on Pro and Growth.

El huésped escribe en japonés y Lio responde en japonés; tú ves la traducción de la respuesta de Lio en tu idioma. Las respuestas que escribes tú se envían tal cual, sin traducción automática.

## Conoce tu hotel
Horarios de check-in y check-out, aparcamiento, política de mascotas, horario del desayuno, transporte y características de las habitaciones. Los introduces una vez y Lio los usa de forma coherente en cada respuesta.

## Un asistente que vende
Lio no solo responde preguntas: ofrece traslados al aeropuerto, visitas por la ciudad y extras en el momento adecuado, y pasa la solicitud a tu equipo.

## Recibe solicitudes de reserva
En los planes Pro y Growth, cuando un huésped pregunta por una habitación en WhatsApp, Lio recoge las fechas, el número de personas y la habitación que prefiere, y le da un precio según tus tarifas y tu disponibilidad. La solicitud te llega a ti y se convierte en reserva cuando la apruebas.

## Sugerencias cada mañana
Cada mañana, las Sugerencias de Lio señalan oportunidades de precio, tareas operativas (habitaciones por limpiar, solicitudes pendientes), ajustes de configuración que faltan y oportunidades de ingresos. Nada cambia sin tu aprobación y las sugerencias de precio no salen de los límites que tú fijas. Incluidas en todos los planes.

## Análisis de reseñas y mensajes
En Pro y Growth, Lio resume los temas de queja y de elogio que se repiten en las reseñas y los mensajes de tus huéspedes. El resumen semanal con IA viene incluido en Growth y es opcional en Pro.

## Tú mantienes el control
Durante los primeros días puedes aprobar las respuestas de Lio antes de que se envíen. Tú decides qué temas cierra Lio por su cuenta y cuáles te pasa a ti.

# Channel manager hotelero para 100+ OTAs | Hostlio Pro
URL: https://hostliopro.com/es/channel-manager/

## Un channel manager para más de 100 OTAs

Gestiona la disponibilidad, las tarifas y las reservas de Booking.com, Airbnb, Expedia, Agoda y más de 100 canales desde un solo calendario. Hostlio Pro sincroniza en tiempo real y en ambos sentidos.

Empieza tu prueba gratuita de 7 días

Canales conectados

Booking.com Sincronizado

Airbnb Sincronizado

Expedia Sincronizado

Agoda Sincronizado

Google Hotels Sincronizado

¿Qué es un channel manager? Un software que mantiene sincronizadas la disponibilidad y las tarifas de un hotel mientras vende habitaciones en varios canales online a la vez. Cuando una habitación se vende en un canal, se cierra al instante en todos los demás, lo que evita las reservas duplicadas (overbooking).

## Qué hace el channel manager

## Sincronización bidireccional
Las nuevas reservas, modificaciones y cancelaciones aparecen automáticamente en el planning de habitaciones, y los cambios que haces en el calendario se envían a todos los canales.

## Tarifas y restricciones
Envía tarifas, estancias mínimas y cierres de venta por tipo de habitación a todos los canales desde una sola pantalla.

## Planning de habitaciones por colores
Ve de un vistazo de qué canal viene cada reserva. Reasigna habitaciones arrastrando y soltando.

## Conectado a la mensajería
Los mensajes de los huéspedes de reservas de OTAs llegan a la bandeja de Lio con el huésped, la habitación y las fechas junto a cada conversación.

## Una temporada entera de una vez
Elige un rango de fechas, los tipos de habitación y los planes tarifarios, y define precio, estancia mínima y máxima, cerrado a la llegada, cerrado a la salida o cierre de ventas. Marca «solo fines de semana» para dar otro precio a las noches de viernes y sábado. Si un canal se desincroniza, «reenviar a los canales» envía de nuevo las tarifas y la disponibilidad actuales.

## Las habitaciones fuera de servicio se cierran solas
Cuando una habitación queda fuera de servicio por una avería, la disponibilidad baja en todos los canales conectados y la habitación no se puede asignar hasta que vuelve a estar operativa. Desactivar un tipo de habitación funciona igual: se envía disponibilidad 0 a todos los canales conectados hasta que lo vuelvas a activar.

## Trae tus reservas actuales
Sube las reservas de tu sistema anterior en CSV o Excel. Las columnas se asignan automáticamente, los duplicados se omiten y las filas con problemas aparecen con el motivo.

Pantalla real del panel de Hostlio Pro (datos de un hotel de demostración)
